properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 1:14AM CST by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
The combination of an upper level storm system, increasing
moisture and temperatures in the 30s may produce a few hours of
light snow mainly west of a Sterling City to Throckmorton line
Tuesday morning. Expect little to no accumulation of snowfall.
However, there is a low chance of local accumulations around 1/2
of an inch which may cause a few slick spots on roads. The rest of
west central Texas will only see rain showers Tuesday morning.
Keep up with the latest weather information this week.

Also, expect colder temperatures across the area. A widespread
freeze is expected Wednesday morning with lows in the mid to upper
20s, possibly a few degrees colder in low lying areas and river
valleys. Highs will only be in the 40s Tuesday. Please prepare
for the colder weather.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides
and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during
periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into
Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

infrastructure.
